purpose: Detection-accuracy check on already-disclosed and already-patched advisories. Each case scans the official released archive of the last vulnerable version, then the first fixed version as a control. No new vulnerabilities are sought; no exploit code is written; the PoC step is off.
hintLevel: L0: no CWE, no file or line, no advisory text, no fix diff and no CVE/GHSA id in any model input.

tool.name: vettalon
tool.build: cargo build --release -p vettalon from the main branch on 2026-10-20

roster.verifierAssignment: one cross-family verifier per finding, rotating between grok and agy (product default)

command: vettalon scan <tree> --profile deep --config roster.toml --finders claude --verifiers grok,agy --max-modules 8 --refuter-runs 1 --no-prior --time-budget 2400 --source-receipts --trace trace.jsonl --report report.json --lang en

fixedParameters.reason: Same parameters for every arm. refuter-runs 1 (product default is 3 for High and above) keeps the per-scan worst case bounded under the 400-call cap.

inputPreparation.source: official registry archive of each version (crates.io .crate, PyPI sdist, proxy.golang.org module zip, npm tarball, Packagist dist zipball), checksum-checked against the registry where it publishes one; top-level directory stripped; no git history.
inputPreparation.exclusions: Applied identically to both arms of a case before scanning: changelog files (CHANGELOG.*, docs/changelog.rst) and any file whose name or content names the advisory (PyJWT 2.4.0 tests/test_advisory.py). Everything else in the archive is scanned as released.
inputPreparation.treeDigest: sha256 over sorted '<file sha256>  <relative path>' lines of the tree after exclusions

budget.perScanWorstCaseDerivation: finder <= 8 modules x (1 + 1 parse retry) = 16; verify <= 60 candidates (run-wide cap) x 1 refuter run = 60; no other model steps run with --poc off and no prescreen
budget.gate: a scan starts only when calls used so far + 76 <= 400; calls are counted from each scan's --trace file plus 1 pre-run model-id probe
budget.stopRules: benchmarks/common/live_guard.py rules: stop when more than 20% of the last 50 calls are errors or refusals; rate-limit rejections are counted separately, the next scan waits the guard cooldown, and rate limiting that persists 15 minutes stops the run. No scan is retried in a loop.
budget.rerun: at most one re-run of an arm, only when more than 20% of its calls failed for infrastructure reasons (rate limit, timeout, CLI error). Both runs are reported.

vulnerableArm.found: a reported AI finding whose file equals the target file, whose line lies inside a target range, whose CWE is in acceptedCwes, and whose final status is not refuted
vulnerableArm.foundButRefuted: as found, but the verifier refuted it; reported separately and not counted as found
vulnerableArm.locationOnly: file and line inside a target range but CWE outside acceptedCwes; reported separately and not counted as found
vulnerableArm.missedReviewed: target file was in the audited coverage and no finding meets found or locationOnly
vulnerableArm.missedNotSelected: target file was not in the audited modules (ranking or page cap), so the model never saw it
vulnerableArm.notRun: budget gate or stop rule prevented the scan

fixedArm.flagged: a finding on the fixed version inside the corresponding fixed range with a CWE in acceptedCwes and status not refuted (a false positive on patched code)
fixedArm.notRun: budget gate or stop rule prevented the scan

outcomes.otherFindings: every other finding is listed by file, line, CWE, severity and status only; it is not reviewed here. Anything that might be a different, unpatched issue is not investigated or published.

excluded: tests/test_advisory.py (fixed arm only; absent from the vulnerable archive)

cases.note: A finding about header-name validation in assertHeader (vulnerable lines 213-234) matches a different, later advisory (GHSA-wxmh-65f7-jcvw, CVE-2023-29197, fixed in 2.4.5). It is recorded as related-different and is not counted as found for this case.
